key_insight: PEA spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects in 2D lead iodide perovskites, slowing degradation under ambient light and thermal stress compared with BA spacers.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires structural and chemical engineering, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compare BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 exfoliated nanoflakes.
Assess ambient photo- and thermal stability using confocal micro-Raman spectroscopy.
Probe chemical degradation using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: Fresh nanoflakes showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based samples degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI2 and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports material-level stability rather than solar-cell efficiency or device lifetime, so device-level benefits remain unverified.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
